learning_outcomes.text: Know the main elements that are part of electrical circuits, and in particular their mathematical models, constructive characteristics, and physical behavior.
Acquire and understand the basic principles governing the behavior of electrical circuits, theorems, and resolution methods.

Understand the concepts of instantaneous, active, reactive, and apparent energy and power, as well as power factor and its correction, in electrical systems and their importance in industrial electrical installations.
Understand and know how to work with single-phase and three-phase systems.
Know the general fundamentals of electrical machines.
Understand the operating principle of transformers.
Understand the principle of electromechanical energy conversion and its main applications (electromagnets, electric brakes, contactors, etc.).
Understand the creation of magnetic field in the air gap and induced electromotive forces in rotating electrical machines in steady state.
Understand the operation of rotating machines as motor and generator.

assessment_methods.method: Tests, assignments, and reports for practical activities

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a written assessment test (80%) and practical activities including tests, assignments, and reports (20%). A minimum grade of 4.0 is required for the written assessment test. The written assessment test is recoverable, while the practical activities are not.
